# Filtered pagination compatibility fixtures

`filtered_tokens_2_17_2.json` contains tokens generated by the unmodified production
filter and list packages at tag `2.17.2`, commit
`2511cdbd74cd531c6633f2e094d235082a32917d`. They use experiment listing with the
default timestamp sort and both V1 and V2 filter messages.

To regenerate, run `generate_legacy_tokens.go` with `go run` from a checkout of
that tag. The generator also accepts a fixture JSON filename to check tokens
against the old reader. Only `name`, `version`, `filter`, and `token` are needed by
the regression test; the other fields record the old reader's behavior.

The compatibility fix restores the current model's case-insensitive filter
metadata before comparing criteria or executing token-only requests. It does not
weaken identifier validation or change predicate equality checks.

Compatibility has limits:

- Old servers ignore the added metadata, so current scalar-string filter tokens
  remain readable by 2.17.2. String `IN` and numeric repeated-filter comparisons
  already fail on 2.17.2 because JSON decoding changes Go value types; this fix
  does not change that old-server behavior or numeric comparison behavior.
- During a mixed-version rollout, old and new servers may use different string
  comparison and ordering semantics. Token acceptance does not guarantee an
  unchanged result set or prevent skipped/duplicate rows in that situation.
  Restart pagination after the rollout when those semantics differ.
- Nullable sort cursors and other sort-field migrations are separate from this
  filter-metadata fix.
